record.paper_title: Open problems for tractability of multivariate integration
record.original_question: For integration of real functions on [0,1]^d whose mixed partial derivatives up to order r(d) are uniformly bounded, if d/r(d) stays bounded as d grows, is the number of function values needed for relative error epsilon not bounded by any polynomial in d and epsilon^{-1}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer d ≥ 1 and integer r ≥ 1, let F_{d,r} denote the class of real-valued functions f on the unit cube [0,1]^d that are r times continuously differentiable and satisfy

  ‖∂^{|α|} f / ∂x^α‖_∞ ≤ 1  for every multi-index α = (α_1,…,α_d) ∈ ℤ_{≥0}^d with |α| = α_1+…+α_d ≤ r.

For ε ∈ (0,1), let n(ε,d,r) denote the minimal number N such that there exists an algorithm using N function values of f which, for every f ∈ F_{d,r}, approximates the integral ∫_{[0,1]^d} f(x) dx with worst-case error at most ε · ‖f‖ (relative error, with a suitable normalization of the class).

Let r : ℕ → ℕ be a function such that the ratio d / r(d) remains bounded as d → ∞. Prove or disprove the following statement: the quantity n(ε,d,r(d)) cannot be bounded above by any polynomial in d and ε^{-1}; that is, multivariate integration over the family of classes F_{d,r(d)} is intractable.
artifact.category_tag: Information-based complexity / tractability of multivariate integration
artifact.status_search_result: Hinrichs, Novak, Ullrich and Woźniakowski (2014, "The curse of dimensionality for numerical integration of smooth functions", Math. Comp.; and Part II) proved the curse of dimensionality for multivariate integration on the classes F_{d,r}: the minimal number of function values needed to reach error ε is at least c_r(1+γ_r)^d. In particular this rules out any polynomial bound in d and ε^{-1} when d/r(d) stays bounded, settling the question in the affirmative (the problem is indeed intractable).

status_evidence.title: The Curse of Dimensionality for Numerical Integration of Smooth Functions
status_evidence.snippet: We prove the curse of dimensionality in the worst case setting for multivariate numerical integration for various classes of smooth functions...
status_evidence.claim: Establishes curse of dimensionality for F_{d,r}-type smoothness classes, implying intractability.

status_evidence.title: The curse of dimensionality for numerical integration of smooth functions II
status_evidence.snippet: the number of function values to achieve error ε is larger than c_r (1+γ)^d
status_evidence.claim: Exponential lower bound in d rules out polynomial tractability when d/r(d) is bounded.
